title: Resumable session locks and lightweight ack façade for Python streaming SDK
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: current Python SDK streaming handlers force callers to manage resume checkpoints, deduplication and ack semantics for partial responses. This leads to brittle app code when connections are interrupted or when clients fan-in/out across workers. Goal: provide a lightweight ack/lock façade and resumable session primitives that make common streaming chat patterns ergonomic without hiding important failure semantics. The façade should make it straightforward to: 1) serialize incremental tokens/events to durable checkpoints, 2) perform idempotent replays, 3) coordinate a single consumer among multiple workers (session lock), and 4) expose observability (watermarks, latency of first byte, retry counts).
design_decisions: Expose a small Session object that owns the connection lifecycle and exposes: .events() async iterator, .checkpoint() manual hook, and .acquire_lock()/release_lock() for short-lived ownership across workers.
Default semantics: optimistic checkpointing every N events (configurable); checkpoints are optional for low-latency callers but recommended for high-reliability flows.
Keep ack model explicit: SDK will provide ack(event_id) and nack(event_id, reason) helpers; automatic ack-on-yield is opt-in via a parameter to the iterator.

Retries: transport-level reconnects should be automatic with a backoff and jitter policy, but SDK will not implicitly re-emit application-level events unless a checkpoint indicates partial consumption.

Do not introduce complex distributed consensus. Session locks are advisory and short-lived; users with strict single-writer requirements should pair the SDK primitive with their durable store (Redis/consul).
Telemetry: emit named spans and counters (session.open, session.resume, checkpoint.write, ack, retry) to the Console.
implementation_notes:
class Session:
    def __init__(..., checkpoint_store: Optional[CheckpointStore]=None, auto_ack: bool=False, lock_timeout: int=30): ...
    async def events(self): yield Event -- async iterator that yields typed events
    async def checkpoint(self, token_cursor: str): write checkpoint to store
    async def acquire_lock(self): advisory lock to coordinate consumer ownership
    async def release_lock(self): release advisory lock
CheckpointStore interface: a pluggable lightweight adapter with get(key), set(key, value, ttl) methods. Provide Redis and in-memory adapters in SDK for easy testing.

Transport reconnection behavior: on socket reconnect, if checkpoint exists for session_id and last_emitted_cursor < server_cursor, then SDK will resume and replay only missing fragments up to checkpoint boundary. It will attach a replay header to request to ensure server-side truncation if supported.
Backpressure: allow an optional max_inflight_events configuration that buffers up to N events and stalls reading from transport to avoid OOM in long-running sessions.
Security: session lock tokens should be ephemeral and stored only in the checkpoint store; do not persist PII in checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes Session API and CheckpointStore adapters in python-sdk v0.23.0-alpha
End-to-end tests for resume semantics covering: clean disconnect, mid-token disconnect, and duplicated replay scenarios
Benchmarks show <5% median extra latency when auto_ack is disabled versus previous streaming API for equivalent workloads
Telemetry events appear in Console under session.* metrics for all CI runs
Documentation + cookbook example demonstrating single-worker and multi-worker consumer patterns
test_plan: Unit: CheckpointStore adapters (in-memory and redis) and lock timing behaviors
Integration: simulated flaky network harness (CI job) that introduces random disconnects and validates exactly-once event delivery when callers use checkpoint+ack patterns
Load: run streaming producer at 300 rps with 1s average token gaps and verify memory/latency under max_inflight_events throttling
Chaos: smoke tests with two consumers racing for same session_id to validate advisory lock semantics (one should be primary)
rollout_plan: Alpha release behind sdk.feature_flags.stream_resumability for customers and internal dogfooding
Collect feedback for two weeks from internal apps (chatbot, docs summarizer) and fix any ergonomic regressions
Graduate API to GA in 3 cycles after addressing outstanding issues and stabilizing telemetry
Provide migration guide: mapping from old stream iterator usage to Session.events() + checkpoint()
Add feature flag gating on server-side resume support; server falls back to cold-start if resume not supported
